attributes.context: This provision appears in Article 14, Union Cooperation, immediately after Section 14.2, where the Union agrees to cooperate with the Employer in installing improved methods and educating members about changes and improvements. It also references Article 15, Automation, which begins by recognizing that technological change involving automated equipment, the Universal Product Code, and electronic checkout equipment is available to the retail food industry.

extraction_text: Section 14.3 In the event that the Employer contemplates the introduction of major technological changes affecting bargaining unit work, advance notice of such change will be given to the Union. If requested to do so, the Employer will meet with the Union to discuss the implementation of such changes before putting such changes into effect. (See Article 15.)

attributes.context: Items E, F, and G in the same chunk address displacement from major technological change and severance pay for installation of such equipment.

extraction_text: A. Where installations of such equipment will materially affect bargaining unit work, the Union will be pre-notified by the Employer sixty (60) days prior to installation.

attributes.context: Item E in the same chunk explicitly links the displacement context to major technological change.

extraction_text: B. The Employer has the right to install such equipment.

attributes.context: The same chunk’s items A, D, E, F, and G discuss installation of such equipment and displacement from major technological change.

extraction_text: C. Any training or necessary retraining will be furnished expense free by the Employer to affected employees.

attributes.context: Item E in the same chunk explicitly states that displacement may result from major technological change.

extraction_text: D. Where employees who average thirty (30) hours or more per week for the preceding eight (8) consecutive weeks would be displaced by such installation, the Employer will make every effort to affect a transfer.

attributes.context: Items F and G in the same chunk set severance pay amounts and calculation for displaced employees.

extraction_text: E. If an employee who averaged thirty (30) hours or more per week for eight (8) consecutive weeks is not re-trained or transferred and would be displaced as a direct result of major technological change, as defined above, then the employee would qualify for separation pay if: 1. The employee (except Utility Clerks) had two (2) or more years of service in which he averaged thirty (30) hours or more per week for eight (8) consecutive weeks. 2. Does not refuse a transfer first to a store within the forty (40) mile radius from home store location and then within the Local Union jurisdiction.. 3. Does not refuse to be retrained. 4. Such action does not occur more than six (6) months from date of installation. 5. Does not voluntarily terminate employment.

attributes.context: Item E in the same chunk links displacement to major technological change, and item G specifies the severance pay calculation.

extraction_text: F. Employees who have averaged thirty (30) or more hours per week within the two (2) years preceding the installation of such equipment would receive severance pay in the amount of one (1) week's pay for each year over two (2) years up to a maximum of eight (8) weeks.

attributes.context: Item F in the same chunk establishes severance pay for installation of such equipment, and item E links the displacement to major technological change.

extraction_text: G. Severance pay would equate the average number of hours worked the four (4) weeks preceding displacement, not to exceed forty (40) hours straight-time pay.

attributes.context: This provision appears under Article 3, Management Rights, and limits the stated management right by reference to Article 14, Section 14.3, and Article 15; those referenced articles are not included in the current chunk.

extraction_text: The management of the business and the direction of the working forces, including the right to plan, direct and control store operations, hire, suspend or discharge for proper cause, transfer or relieve employees from duty because of lack of work or other legitimate reasons, the right to study or introduce new or improved production methods or facilities (subject to the provisions of Article 14, Section 14.3 and Article 15) and the right to establish and maintain rules and regulations covering the operation of the stores, a violation of which shall be among the causes for discharge, are vested in the Employer; provided, however, that this right shall be exercised with due regard for the rights of the employees, and provided further that it will not be used for the purpose of discrimination against any employee.
